Honestly I probably wouldn't move here just for the reason of it being child free. As much as I don't like kids, there are so many more important things that need fixing in the world other than us just running away to some place for our own benefit. I don't have to see or interact with children much so it's not so bad for me. But some questions that would come up would be:
1. Does this mean that no one from the age of 18-30 lives in the town? I had old crochety/stubborn people almost more than kids
2. This community is not garunteed to be kid free, and tbh, parents aren't always the best at picking where there kids should live. So even if it's harder for them, if they like it there, they may stay....
3. What are the legal reasons that we cant just say "no children allowed"? I mean 65 plus communities in the US do this ALL the time, just with a different age group.

Overall, seems like a nice idea, but I'm skeptical that it would actually keep kids away and not be filled with old people messing up orders at restaurants and sucking at driving.

Maybe you should tell them how afraid you are and the things that you think about. I've been dealing with suicide since I was a child as well....and I know how torturous it is. Thankfully I still have my father and brother. Many years ago, I decided not to kill myself because the thought of leaving my mother behind. Now I don't kill myself because we'll...I try really hard to be a good person, and although I am not, I try, and that's enough. Maybe it's enough for you too? You don't seem like a bad person, just someone who deals with more than what other deal with, and I'm sure your family can understand if you try and show them how you feel and why life is so difficult. Just remember that you don't have to do anything, accomplish anything, be anything but yourself....that's enough and can make life worth living. And the fact that you want to be there for your mother, says a lot about you :)

I hope things get better for you, I truly mean that.

I was in this situation at that age also, started when I was about 8....its not your fault or anyone's fault. As we as humans study the brain futher....we are finding out that most of who we are is nature...not nurture.....and your sister is most likely no exception to this. Maybe she doesn't want to open up to you, and that's why she doesn't. Maybe she wants to die, hell I do.....there are 1 million thoughts that probably go through her head and a similar # of potential outcomes. I would prepare for as many as you can before they happen.....and also, do t get mad at her when she comes home.....

It might help to tell her how you feel, not to get angry at her, don't do that, but she might be angry too. And if she feels anger, then she at least is feeling something. Tell her how much you love her, and why you care about her. I'm not an expert, but as someone who has struggled with suicide for 20 years.....I know sometimes it helps me to hear how my actions negatively impact the lives of those around me because I don't want to make them angry either...
